Article Title: 'Uniform ke peeche bhi ek insaan hai': Delhi Police issues 'open letter' to protesters
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Delhi Police has issued an open letter to citizens, emphasising that protecting their safety is its responsibility and that police personnel, despite wearing uniforms, are human beings with families and loved ones."Dear citizen, Aapki awaaz aapka haq hai, aur aapki surakhsha hamara farz. Uniform ke peeche bhi ek insaan hai, jiska aapna Parivar hai, apne log hai. Farq sirf uniform ka hai, insaaniyat ka nahi," the letter read.(Your voice is your right, and your safety is our duty. Behind the uniform is also a human being, who has a family and loved ones. The only difference is the uniform, not humanity).The open letter comes amid heightened tensions over protests in the national capital after the Delhi Police denied permission for the Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) proposed demonstration at Jantar Mantar on October 10. The police cited the late submission of its application, non-compliance with rules during a previous demonstration and concerns over public safety, law and order, and traffic management.Joint Commissioner of Police Nupur Prasad said the New Delhi district police received an application from CJP co-convenor Saurabh Das on October 7, seeking permission to hold a protest demanding accountability from Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“On October 7, 2026, an application from Saurabh Das, Co-Convenor of the Cockroach Janata Party, was received in the New Delhi District. As per the application, an intimation was given regarding a protest to be held at Jantar Mantar on October 10 concerning the accountability of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC). Upon processing this intimation, it was found that the notice was received at very short notice. Under current guidelines, an application to organise an event at Jantar Mantar must be submitted at least 10 days prior to the scheduled date,” Prasad said.Meanwhile, Delhi Police on Monday issued an advisory for journalists covering protests, asking them to carry valid identity cards issued by their respective organisations or PIB/DIP accreditation cards and keep them visibly displayed to facilitate identification by law enforcement personnel.The advisory urged media personnel to ensure their presence and activities did not obstruct police operations or the movement of security personnel. Journalists were also advised to maintain a reasonable and safe distance while covering and recording proceedings during tense situations.They were further asked to position themselves in a manner that clearly distinguished them from protesters, particularly at crowded sites where police personnel are deployed. The police said the measures were intended to facilitate the identification of journalists and prevent interference with police operations.
Article Summary: The open letter comes amid heightened tensions over protests in the national capital. Delhi Police denied permission for the Cockroach Janata Party’s (CJP) proposed demonstration at Jantar Mantar on October 10. The police cited the late submission of its application, non-compliance with rules during a previous demonstration and concerns over public safety.

Article Title: Plane hit, pilot killed: Riyadh airport attacks by Houthi kill three, damages Saudia aircraft
Article Text:
Riyadh airport attacks kill 3 Saudis, pilot; Saudia aircraft damaged

Three Saudi nationals were killed and several others injured in two attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and a Saudia Airlines aircraft on Thursday, Saudi Arabia’s general authority of civil aviation said on Friday.The first attack targeted airport facilities, while the second struck the aircraft, the authority said. It did not identify those responsible, although Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen claimed to have targeted the airport, as cited by AP.Saudia Airlines has confirmed that a pilot was killed and an aircraft was damaged in the attack.Operations at King Khalid International Airport have since resumed, with air traffic returning to normal, according to the civil aviation authority.The attacks come amid a heightened security situation in Saudi Arabia following separate strikes on Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport on October 6 and 7. Those attacks left three people dead and 36 injured, according to the authority. Two people were killed and 28 injured at Abha airport, while one person was killed and eight injured at King Khalid International Airport.Saudi Civil Defence personnel responded to Thursday’s incident after a missile was launched by the Houthi militia, the Saudi Civil Defence said.Following the attacks on civilian facilities, Saudi-led coalition forces said they had destroyed 82 military targets belonging to the Houthi militia in Yemen.Amid the security situation, the Indian Embassy in Riyadh on Thursday advised Indian nationals in Saudi Arabia to remain vigilant, stay indoors when necessary and follow instructions issued by local authorities through official channels.“In view of the current situation, all Indian nationals in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia are advised to remain alert and vigilant, stay indoors as necessary, and follow the instructions issued by local authorities through official channels. Indian nationals are strongly advised to refrain from circulating or reposting any videos or news related to the ongoing events," the embassy said in an advisory.The mission said the Embassy of India in Riyadh and the Consulate in Jeddah, including their outsourced services through VFS, continued to operate normally and would issue further updates as required."The Embassy of India, Riyadh and the Consulate in Jeddah and its outsourced services through VFS, are continuing to function normally and will issue updates and advisories as and when necessary. The 24x7 helpline of Pravasi Bharatiya Sahayata Kendra (PBSK) remains available on Toll free No: 8002471234,” it added.India on Thursday condemned the attacks on the two Saudi airports, calling the targeting of civilian infrastructure “completely unacceptable”.In a statement, the Ministry of External Affairs said, “India condemns the attacks over the past few days targeting Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which have resulted in civilian deaths and injuries.”“The targeting of civilian infrastructure is completely unacceptable,” the MEA said, expressing condolences to the families of those killed and wishing those injured a speedy recovery.
Article Summary: Three Saudi nationals killed and several others injured in two attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen claimed to have targeted the airport. Saudi-led coalition forces said they had destroyed 82 military targets belonging to the Houthi militia in Yemen.

NEW DELHI: Additional DCP New Delhi Manjeet Sheoran on Friday urged journalists to maintain a distance from protesters while covering demonstrations. He alleged that some media personnel join protests and obstruct police work."Some protestors come one day as a journalist and come the other day as a protestor. We keep appealing to them that you keep a little distance from the protestors, cover it from a distance. Article Title: J&K: PDP leader detained after calling terrorist Burhan Wani a 'martyr'
Article Text: NEW DELHI: PDP leader Abdul Kabir referred to Hizbul Mujahideen terrorist Burhan Wani as a "martyr" during a speech at an event in Jammu and Kashmir.He was later detained in Kishtwar for questioning over the remark.Earlier, news agency ANI asked Kabir about his use of the term "martyr" for the slain terrorist. He was a posterboy of the Hizbul Mujahideen terrorist group.

Article Title: Supreme Court: For post-split suicide, can't always accuse ex of abetment
Article Text:
File photo: Supreme Court

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court has held that when the break-up of a relationship ends in suicide, it cannot always be termed abetment and a former partner prosecuted.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran quashed criminal proceedings against a man and five of his family members who were being prosecuted for abetment after his live-in partner died by suicide after they broke up."People react differently to situations and if a breakup ends up with suicide, it cannot always be termed an abetment to suicide. The refusal to marry was not with an intention to drive the woman to death by suicide nor can knowledge be attributed to the accused that on such refusal, she would die by suicide," the bench said.The couple had been living together for a few mo-nths before the relationship ended. The woman's relative lodged a case against the man and five of his family members, including his parents."We are unable to find any instigation by the accused/appellants to drive the deceased to death by suicide. It was neither intended nor can it be said to be abetment. At worst, even if we fully believe what has been stated by the first informant, there was a refusal of marriage, which led to the woman committing suicide," it noted.
Article Summary: A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran quashed criminal proceedings against a man and five of his family members. The man's live-in partner died by suicide after they broke up. The couple had been living together for a few mo-nths before the relationship ended.

Article Title: Group of 42 ex-judges defends SIR, slams opposition attack on Election Commission
Article Text:
File photo: Opposition's anti-SIR stir

NEW DELHI: A group of 42 retired judges on Thursday slammed the opposition's attack on Election Commission , claiming that it appeared to be a calculated campaign driven by "vested political interests" with little regard for the potentially devastating consequences of destabilising the world's largest democracy."India's constitutional bodies are under sustained attack. EC stands at the centre of this assault. Even the higher judiciary, which we hold in high esteem, and statutory agencies have not been spared. These attacks are not reasoned critique," they said in an open letter.Former Supreme Court judges Hemant Gupta and Pankaj Mittal and several former chief justices of high courts, besides retired judges of various HCs were signatories to the statement, which defended the EC's Special Intensive Review (SIR) of electoral rolls, arguing that a clean roll protected every genuine vote.They said they held no brief for any political party but in moments like these, silence was no longer a neutral choice. Constitutional authorities were now branded "thieves", "puppets" and "compromised" from public platforms, they said in a reference to EC's sharp criticism by opposition functionaries and organisations like CJP.Targeting Congress, they said: "EVMs are blamed only after defeat. Victories won on the same machines go unquestioned.A party that governed this nation for over five decades now claims that the very system which elected it is rigged."They said activist outfits with a long record of selective litigation lent these claims a veneer of legality. "They file petitions one after the other. They seldom file proof. The courtroom becomes a stage, and when the judgement is delivered, it is criticised whenever it does not serve their interests."The uproar over SIR appeared both sudden and remarkably convenient, the judges said. "Tell citizens often enough that their vote does not count, and they stop believing in the ballot. When the ballot loses meaning, the street gains it. Unrest begins with a narrative. Anarchic and fringe elements then occupy the vacuum," the group said.While some of these groups were homegrown, some took their cues from beyond borders, they alleged. They appealed to political parties to not delegitimise elections and take their grievances to EC and the courts with evidence.
Article Summary: 42 retired judges slam the opposition's attack on Election Commission. They say it appeared to be a calculated campaign driven by "vested political interests" They say they held no brief for any political party but in moments like these, silence was no longer a neutral choice.

Article Title: Jammu and Kashmir: High court orders passport revival for student purusing MBBS in Iran
Article Text:
Representative image

SRINAGAR: Jammu & Kashmir High Court ordered Thursday revival of Kashmir student’s passport so that she can complete her MBBS in Iran.The authorities had impounded Ibra Khan ’s passport based on a CID adverse report about an FIR against her father in 1997, although she was born in 2005. The report cited “aspersions” against Khan’s father in relation to the case and “apprehensions that she may join anti-India forces”.“This court has the highest concern towards the security of the country. In a very limited intervention and keeping in view that the appellant (student) has completed half her MBBS, we dispose of the appeal by directing that the passport be revived for the remaining period of her course,” a division bench of Chief Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Wasim Sadiq Nargal said.Khan is pursuing MBBS at Tehran University of Medical Sciences. She was issued a passport in Oct 2024 but received showcause notices March 27, 2026 and April 9, 2026 from passport authorities over her father’s case before her passport was impounded on May 4, 2026.Khan moved the HC but a single-judge bench dismissed her petition saying it found no reason to interfere in the decision by authorities and citing an alternative remedy of appeal under Passports Act, 1967.Khan then approached the division bench. Her counsel Salih Pirzada argued that she began pursuing MBBS in 2024 but owing to the prevailing turmoil in the region, she returned to India. It was during this period that she received the notices, followed by the passport’s impounding without clear reasons.J&K’s additional advocate-general (AAG) cited the adverse CID report and claimed Khan had not replied to the show-cause notices, leaving authorities with no alternative but to impound the passport.Following this, the division bench of Justices Bhati and Nargal called for the CID report, which cited the case against Khan’s father and “apprehensions” about the security and sovereignty of the country.Khan’s counsel Pirzada contended that the state had not been able to pinpoint the reasons for such apprehensions given that the case against her father dated to 1997 whereas she herself was born eight years later.The division bench eventually allowed Khan’s appeal by ordering the passport’s revival, saying the authorities were free to impose conditions and directing her to comply with any such riders.
Article Summary: Ibra Khan is pursuing MBBS at Tehran University of Medical Sciences. Her passport was impounded based on a CID adverse report about an FIR against her father in 1997. The report cited “aspersions” against Khan’s father in relation to the case and “apprehensions that she may join anti-India forces”

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK, claiming that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position in the Maduranthakam constituency.Arjuna said the DMK had earlier claimed it would win 200 constituencies but was now sitting in the opposition benches.“The DMK, which said that it would win 200 constituencies, is sitting in the Opposition benches. They took us lightly. They said, ‘These people only know how to blow whistles.’ That very whistle came to us as our symbol, and we have blown them away completely with that whistle,” he said.Arjuna further claimed that the DMK was in a “pathetic position” in the constituency and questioned whether the party would even be able to retain its election deposit.“In this constituency, the DMK is in a pathetic position. Will the DMK even get its deposit back?” he said.He also targeted Tamil Nadu leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin , alleging that his remarks were damaging the DMK.“Everything that comes out of the mouth of Udhayanidhi is only obscenity. No one else needs to come to destroy the DMK; MK Stalin’s son is enough. Udhayanidhi Stalin has come to destroy the DMK,” Arjuna said.Bypolls to the Maduranthakam Assembly constituency in Chengelpet district, adjoining Chennai, and the Dharapuram constituency in Tiruppur district of western Tamil Nadu will be held on October 6.The bypolls were necessitated after AIADMK legislators Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama resigned from their posts and joined the ruling TVK. The party has fielded both of them from the same constituencies they represented after being elected in the April Assembly election.This is the first time the TVK government is facing Assembly bypolls since it assumed office in May 2026.The Left parties, which extend outside support to the TVK government and help it retain its majority, have not joined the ruling party-led alliance. Instead, they are contesting the bypolls as a separate front.Candidates of the main opposition DMK, the AIADMK and the Tamil nationalist Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK) are also in the fray.The Vanniyar-dominated PMK, which has considerable influence in several northern parts of the state, has not extended support to any party.A key opposition campaign plank is that the bypolls were not a natural outcome but were forced on voters after the TVK “lured AIADMK MLAs” to strengthen its numbers in the Assembly.AIADMK chief Edappadi K Palaniswami has already begun campaigning, seeking “justice” over what he has described as the betrayal.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK. He claimed that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position. Bypolls to the Maduranthakam Assembly constituency in Chengelpet district, adjoining Chennai, will be held on October 6.

Article Title: Flydubai cockpit attack: Israel to honour Indian pilot Smit Machchhar with top civilian bravery award
Article Text:
Indian pilot Smit Machchhar to receive Israel’s Presidential Award for Civil Heroism

Six Israeli passengers honoured for thwarting attack

What happened aboard the flydubai flight?

Netanyahu had invited pilot to Israel's Independence Day event

Israel will honour Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar with the Presidential Award for Civil Heroism for his role in preventing a major aviation disaster aboard a flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv, President Isaac Herzog announced on Thursday.Herzog made the announcement while presenting the Presidential Medal for Civilian Heroism to six Israeli passengers who helped thwart the alleged attempt to crash flight FZ1073 last week.The ceremony was held in Jerusalem.“Alongside the Israeli heroes we honor today, we send our heartfelt wishes for a full and speedy recovery to Captain Smit Machchhar of India. Captain Machchhar’s courage, bravery and professionalism helped prevent this catastrophe,” Herzog said.“Once he regains his strength, it will be an honour and a privilege for me to present him, on behalf of the people of Israel, with the Presidential State of Israel Award for Civil Heroism,” he added.The announcement came as Machchhar continued to recover in a hospital in Abu Dhabi after sustaining serious injuries during an alleged attack by his co-pilot inside the aircraft's cockpit.Herzog presented the civilian heroism award to Tali Manes, Zvika Manes, Yaniv Hayoun, Dr Shota Musayev, Asaf Rajuan and Or Pardilov for their roles in preventing the alleged hijacking attempt, according to The Jerusalem Post and The Times of Israel.Tali Manes was credited with first raising the alarm, while Hayoun, Zvika Manes, Pardilov and Rajuan helped subdue the co-pilot after he allegedly attacked the captain. Musayev, a doctor, provided medical assistance to the injured pilot.“Today we gather in Jerusalem to honour six seemingly ordinary Israelis who proved to be extraordinary human beings, true heroes, by saving the flight last week,” Herzog said.“Thanks to their courage, determination and remarkable presence of mind, these heroes prevented a devastating aviation disaster that would have shocked the entire world and saved 174 precious lives.”The Israeli president also expressed gratitude to the replacement pilots who took over the aircraft and other passengers who helped during the emergency.Herzog said the passengers' actions could not remove the need for a full investigation into the incident.“The civilian bravery and resourcefulness demonstrated by the heroes gathered here cannot absolve us of the obligation to obtain full answers,” he said.The incident occurred last week aboard flydubai flight FZ1073, which was carrying 174 passengers to Israel. The co-pilot, identified as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami, allegedly attacked Machchhar with a crash axe inside the cockpit and attempted to take control of the aircraft.The aircraft transmitted emergency signals and made a rapid descent of more than 17,000 feet, from 34,000 feet, before making an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. The UAE subsequently classified the incident as an attempted terrorist attack.Machchhar received initial treatment in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, before being shifted to Abu Dhabi for further medical care.Ministry of external affairs said on Tuesday that the pilot was recovering well and responding positively to treatment. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the Indian embassy in the UAE was in regular contact with Machchhar, his family and hospital authorities.“Captain Smit Machchhar is in the hospital in Abu Dhabi. Our embassy in the UAE has been in regular touch with him, with his family, with local authorities, and with the hospital authorities. He's recuperating well. He's responding well. And his health is improving,” Jaiswal said.Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had earlier spoken to Machchhar while he was receiving treatment in the UAE and praised his actions during the incident.Netanyahu invited the Indian pilot and Prime Minister Narendra Modi to light a flame at Israel's Independence Day event, describing Machchhar as a hero of Israel, India and the world.“It's our highest honour that we give on our Independence Day. It's usually reserved for Israeli citizens, but I think here in this case, all the citizens of Israel will embrace you. They do now, and they will then too. So we hope to see you very soon in Israel,” Netanyahu told the pilot.The Israeli president's announcement on Thursday means Machchhar will also receive a civilian heroism award once he has recovered sufficiently to travel.Herzog established the Presidential Medal for Civilian Heroism following the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack on Israel.The award recognises civilians who display extraordinary courage while putting themselves at genuine risk to save others.
Article Summary: Six Israeli passengers honoured for thwarting attack on flydubai flight. Indian pilot Smit Machchhar to receive Israel’s Presidential Award for Civil Heroism. President Isaac Herzog presented the Presidential Medal for Civilian Heroism to six Israeli passengers who helped thwart the alleged attempt to crash flight FZ1073.

Article Title: Indian-origin doctor mom arrested and charged in Florida as she watched 7-year-old drown. She said she froze, she was not strong enough to pull him from water
Article Text:
Indian-origin doctor mom arrested and charged in Florida for a child's drowning under her watch.

Seven minutes and two seconds

7 days later, Khushil was dead

A Louisiana doctor, Sukanthini Subbiah, has been arrested by the Orlando Police Department in Florida and charged with first-degree aggravated manslaughter as she was present when seven-year-old Khushil Bandi drowned. The incident took place on April 10 but the arrest was made on Wednesday. The 48-year-old Indian-origin doctor is being held without bond in the Orange County Jail and she faces up to 30 years in prison if convicted.Subbiah was visiting her mother in Orlando with her own seven-year-old son identified as DJ by the police. DJ became friends with Khushil and his twin sister who lived in the neighborhood. Khushil and his twin sister were supposed to be under Subbaiah and her mother's watch one evening and they went to a pool. Immediately, the three children jumped into the pool. Subbaiah told the police that she noticed that Khushil had been underwater for 45 seconds or so. She asked the other two to look for him but they said the water was too deep. Subbaiah sought help from another man who jumped into the water and pulled out Khushil, who was unconscious at the time.Subbiah said she did not waste any time but surveillance footage revealed that she did not do anything for a long time.Surveillance footage revealed that they arrived at the pool at 6.19 pm. At 6.20 pm, Khushil could be seen playing in the pool and Subbiah was not seen in the footage. Seven seconds later, Subbiah was seen in the footage. About a minute later, Khushil sank to the bottom of the pool. After another minute and half, Subbiah went to the edge of the water and was seen "standing and staring at the center of the pool". For another minute, she did not do anything and then asked his son what happened to Khushil.Three minutes later, Subbiah got into the water but stopped at knee height.Then she approached another man for help. The man jumped and brought Khushil in 50 seconds. The total time between the boy being completely submerged and being removed from the water was seven minutes and two seconds, police said.Khushil was rushed to a hospital in a critical condition. After three days, he had no brain activity and he had swelling in his brain and was suffering from seizures. He was taken off life support on April 17 and pronounced dead. An autopsy report concluded that his cause of death was ruled as complications of drowning.When police interviewed Subbiah, she allegedly said that she 'froze' and thought she was 'going to pass out' after noticing Khushil had been submerged for an extended period. She also allegedly said she believed she was not strong enough to pull the seven-year-old from the water, which is why she asked for help.Investigators concluded that Subbiah had the opportunity to alter the outcome.
Article Summary: Sukkanthini Subbiah, 48, is being held without bond in the Orange County Jail and she faces up to 30 years in prison if convicted. The incident took place on April 10 but the arrest was made on Wednesday. Khushil was taken off life support on April 17 and pronounced dead. An autopsy report concluded that his cause of death was ruled as complications of drowning.

Article Title: 'This is emergency': 10,000 detained across India ahead of Delhi's Jantar Mantar stir, says CJP
Article Text:
Dipke questioned the restrictions on the planned demonstration, responding to a video of activists being detained.

(With inputs from PTI)





NEW DELHI: At least 10,000 people have been detained across the country ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's ( CJP ) planned protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on October 10, the party's spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed on Friday.The CJP said those detained included students from Pune who were travelling to Delhi to participate in the protest. According to the party, the students were being taken away in a bus to an unknown location.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned the restrictions on the planned demonstration, responding to a video of activists being detained with the remark: "Why not just declare EMERGENCY?" (sic)"At least 10000 people have been detained across the country across (Cockroach Janta Party), various student orgs, Kisaan and Dalit Sangathans, political parties. THIS IS EMERGENCY," Ranka said in a post on X. (sic)Also read: CJP Protest Live Updates Among those detained was national spokesperson Deepak Baliyan, who was taken into police custody on Thursday and released later that night, the party said.The detentions came ahead of the CJP's planned march to Jantar Mantar to demand the scrapping of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and accountability for the alleged deletion of voters.Dipke had called for a nationwide mobilisation against the exercise, saying the protest would proceed even if the party's leaders were detained or arrested.Addressing a press conference on Thursday, he criticised restrictions on public gatherings in the national capital and questioned why protests could be held in Mumbai and Bengaluru but not in Delhi."Jantar Mantar belongs to people of India, it does not belong to Union Home Minister Amit Shah," he said."If Mumbai and Bengaluru can have peaceful protests, why is Amit Shah not allowing it in Delhi?" the CJP founder asked.Dipke urged political parties, civil society groups and social activists to unite to protect voting rights. He alleged that large numbers of voters had been deleted from electoral rolls and questioned the Election Commission's role in the exercise."SIR is the biggest scam that the central government, the BJP-ruled government, is pulling off to kill democracy in India," he said.Referring to testimonies of people allegedly declared dead in electoral records despite producing Aadhaar, PAN and other valid documents to establish that they were alive, Dipke questioned how living voters could be marked dead and removed from the rolls.He alleged that the BJP and the Election Commission were working together to delete the votes of people who did not support the ruling party. The Election Commission's role and the allegations made by the CJP could not be independently established from the party's claims.Dipke also cited alleged deletions in constituencies associated with opposition leaders, including former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, Tamil Nadu chief minister M K Stalin and former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal. He questioned whether the cases were coincidental or pointed to a pattern."If we believe that there is no involvement of the BJP with the Election Commission, then why is it always the opposition leaders who lose? And why does it always benefit the BJP?" he asked.He described the process as "unconstitutional", arguing that it undermined the principle that people should choose their government rather than the government determining who could vote."The government is selecting who will be the voter and who will not vote," he said.The CJP founder said the October 10 march would seek to hold Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Centre accountable for the alleged deletion of votes. He also urged Delhi Police to learn from Karnataka Police how to protect people's rights.Dipke criticised PM Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah, saying they did not own the country or Jantar Mantar and were only "servants with a fixed tenure to serve people".He said the party was not seeking to destabilise the country but wanted accountability over the alleged electoral irregularities.CJP spokesperson Saurav Das alleged that party members and young participants in the movement were facing "mass detentions" in several states, including Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Delhi."None of us are afraid of arrests or detentions. The protest has to go on with or without us," he said.Actor Prakash Raj, who addressed a gathering in Bengaluru earlier, said civil society organisations in Karnataka had spent nearly a year documenting alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise and had presented their findings in different parts of the country.He said testimonies presented at a tribunal, including those of people allegedly declared dead in electoral records, showed that the issue extended beyond Karnataka.Raj appealed to the media to focus on SIR and expressed solidarity with young protesters travelling to Delhi for the October 10 demonstration. He said Karnataka's civil society groups also supported them.He added that the movement had grown from a Karnataka-based campaign into a broader national struggle, thanking the organisations and young activists involved in documenting alleged irregularities and bringing affected voters before the tribunal.
Article Summary: At least 10,000 people have been detained across the country ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's planned protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on October 10. The CJP said those detained included students from Pune who were travelling to Delhi to participate in the protest. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned the restrictions on the planned demonstration.

Article Title: ‘Leaving with so much love in my heart’: Abhijeet Dipke thanks Bengaluru for giving him ‘a home to return to’
Article Text:
He also thanked Prakash Raj and Aafreen Nawaz for inviting him and introducing him to what he described as Bengaluru’s warmth and generosity.

Calls for nationwide mobilisation against SIR

(With agency inputs)





NEW DELHI: CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke on Friday expressed gratitude for the warmth and affection he received during his two-day visit to Bengaluru, saying he was leaving the city with a new family and a home to return to.In a post on X, Dipke said he was overwhelmed by the kindness he had experienced and thanked Kavitha Lankesh, Esha Lankesh, actor Prakash Raj and his elder sister Aafreen Nawaz for making his visit memorable.“Leaving Bengaluru with so much love in my heart. The warmth, affection and kindness I’ve received over the last two days have been truly overwhelming,” he wrote."Sending a big hug to my new family, Kavitha Lankesh and Esha Lankesh. I came here as a stranger and am leaving with a family I know I’ll keep coming back to, " he wrote.He also thanked Prakash Raj and Aafreen Nawaz for inviting him and introducing him to what he described as Bengaluru’s warmth and generosity.“You’ve all given me more than just beautiful memories. You’ve given me a home to return to,” Dipke added.Dipke called for nationwide mobilisation against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise and announced that the CJP would march to Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on October 10, demanding that the exercise be scrapped and accountability fixed for the alleged deletion of voters.Addressing a press conference on Thursday, the CJP founder said the agitation would go ahead even if the party’s leaders were detained or arrested.Dipke also criticised the Centre for restricting public gatherings in the national capital, questioning why peaceful protests were possible in Mumbai and Bengaluru but not in Delhi.“Jantar Mantar belongs to people of India, it does not belong to Union Home Minister Amit Shah,” Dipke told news agency PTI.“If Mumbai and Bengaluru can have peaceful protests, why is Amit Shah not allowing it in Delhi?” he asked.The CJP leader urged political parties, civil society groups and social activists to unite to protect voting rights. He alleged that large numbers of voters had been deleted during the SIR exercise and questioned the Election Commission’s role.
Article Summary: CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke expresses gratitude for the warmth and affection he received during his two-day visit to Bengaluru. He also thanked Prakash Raj and Aafreen Nawaz for inviting him and introducing him to what he described as Bengaluru’s warmth and generosity. He called for nationwide mobilisation against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.

Article Title: Dalits forced to fall at dominant caste people’s feet to bury kin near Erode in Tamil Nadu
Article Text:
Perundurai tahsildar C Selvakumar told TOI that he has sent a preliminary report to district collector S Kandasamy.

Poll Vote & Share your view What is the most important step to prevent caste-based discrimination? Strict enforcement of anti-discrimination laws Greater public awareness and education 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





ERODE: Dalits of a village near Perundurai in Erode district were forced to fall at the feet of non – dalit residents to get access to a common burial ground for their relative’s funeral on Oct 5, villagers have complained.Perundurai tahsildar C Selvakumar told TOI that he has sent a preliminary report to district collector S Kandasamy. Erode Superintendent of Police D V Kiran Shruti told TOI that, based on a complaint lodged by revenue officials, Thingalur police have registered a case against a few members of the dominant community in the village under provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. "Additional sections will be incorporated based on the findings of the inquiry," she said, adding that Gobichettipalayam DSP Srinivasan has been entrusted with the investigation.The incident occurred in Perumpalli, where dalits have been using a burial ground four kms away in Thingalur panchayat since they were refused access to the common burial ground by residents from the dominant caste.After the demise of Senni (90), father of Kaliyappan, on October 5, dalits decided to take the body to the common burial ground as the one in Thingalur had run out of space.Anticipating resistance from non dalits, Senni’s family had informed the police. Police personnel too arrived at the village, along with revenue officials and village panchayat staff.However, when they were taking the body towards the common burial ground, a bunch of non dalit residents led by Rithuvarman blocked their way, saying dalits cannot be buried there, alleged dalits.Despite repeated pleas from the dalits, Rithuvarman and residents from the dominant caste refused to yield. Dalits alleged that all the while, police personnel stood as mute spectators.“In a desperate attempt to ensure a decent burial, two of us fell at the feet of the non – dalits and pleaded for permission to bury the body,’’ said M Kumar, a dalit. He alleged that no action was taken by the police to prevent the humiliation.Perundurai tahsildar said the family finally buried the body at the common ground after the intervention of officials.“We are inquiring into the allegations of some residents being forced to fall at the feet of some others,” Selvakumar said.
Article Summary: Dalits of a village near Perundurai in Erode district were forced to fall at the feet of non – dalit residents to get access to a common burial ground for their relative’s funeral. The incident occurred in Perumpalli, where dalits have been using a burial ground four kms away in Thingalur panchayat since they were refused access.

Article Title: Mumbai man poisons daughter’s biryani for opposing his remarriage, kills her
Article Text:
Khan tried to pass it off as a case of food poisoning, but doctors observed the strangulation marks on the neck leading to his arrest.





MUMBAI: A 45-year-old carpenter killed his 20-year-old daughter by poisoning her chicken biryani and later strangled her after she and her sister objected to his remarriage. He had intended to kill her second daughter too, but she escaped since she decided to stay with her uncle on the fateful night.The incident happened on Oct 2.The Wadala police on Wednesday arrested Sharif Raza Hussain Khan for the murder of Rifat; he has been remanded to police custody. She became unconscious when he strangled her to death, said police.Khan tried to pass it off as a case of food poisoning, but doctors observed the strangulation marks on the neck leading to his arrest.Sharif Khan was living with his daughters Rifat, 20, Nuzhat, 16, and 10-year-old son Ahmed in Madonna Colony, Sheikh Mistry Dargah Road, Wadala East. Rifat’s mother had died of cancer in Nov 2025. Rifat and Nuzhat allegedly opposed the move, leading to frequent arguments. Rifat, in particular, was strongly opposed to her father’s remarriage, police said.On Oct 2, the complainant, Rifat’s maternal uncle Abu Khan was in Ludhiana when he received a call informing him that Rifat had died. He was told that Rifat and Nuzhat had eaten biryani brought home by Sharif before going to sleep on the terrace.Nuzhat later left for her aunt Gausia’s house as it was too humid.At around 5am on Oct 3, Sharif allegedly went to Gausia’s house and told her that Rifat was unresponsive. Relatives then took her to a hospital, where doctors declared her dead.“Khan behaved strangely and took her to KEM hospital. As it was a police case, doctors performed a post-mortem and noted evidence of asphyxia with ligature compression of the neck, with samples preserved for histopathological examination and chemical analysis,’’ said an officer. Based on circumstances and post-mortem findings, police arrested Sharif.
Article Summary: Sharif Raza Hussain Khan arrested for the murder of his 20-year-old daughter Rifat. Khan tried to pass it off as a case of food poisoning, but doctors observed the strangulation marks on the neck leading to his arrest. He had intended to kill her second daughter too, but she escaped.

Article Title: No toilet, TN woman goes to field in ‘model’ Swachh Bharat village, killed by boar
Article Text:
The death has raised questions over sanitation claims in Ariyanendal, which govt showcased as a ‘model village’ under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen).





MADURAI: A 56-year-old woman died after reportedly being attacked by a boar while she was relieving herself in scrubland in Ramanathapuram district.The death has raised questions over sanitation claims in Ariyanendal, which govt showcased as a ‘model village’ under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen).Since her home had no toilet and community facilities were unusable, M Kaali Muthu, an anganwadi worker from Ariyanendal, went outside around 9pm on Tuesday.When she did not return home for more than an hour, her husband, Murali, and other relatives began searching the fields behind their house. Around 10.45pm, they found her lying dead in a pool of blood among the scrub.An investigating officer said the woman’s right thigh had injuries that appeared to have been inflicted by a wild boar. “However, we can confirm the cause of death only after a postmortem report is received,” the officer added.Police registered a case and sent her body to Paramakudi government hospital for postmortem.Police and forest officials are investigating the circumstances of the death.Boars regularly stray through the thickets behind the woman’s home, where invasive prosopis juliflora trees grow amid dense scrub, residents said.It may be recalled that the rural sanitation programme’s 2022 ‘success story’ was presented as an example for other villages to follow.Govt acknowledged toilet coverage was just 10% before 2012, when residents defecated near prosopis thickets amid outbreaks of waterborne diseases.The District Rural Development Agency said it cleared 23 acres of scrubland and launched extensive tree planting to create a ‘beautiful forest’.“This initiative took away the open defecation areas traditionally used by villagers in their vicinity. People began to use the toilets that were constructed,” the mission’s blog said. Govt records list nearly Rs 63 lakh in estimated drainage and soak-pit works under multiple schemes.
Article Summary: A 56-year-old woman died after reportedly being attacked by a boar while she was relieving herself in scrubland in Ramanathapuram district. The death has raised questions over sanitation claims in Ariyanendal, which govt showcased as a ‘model village’ under Swachh Bharat Mission.

Article Title: A plan for every protest: Inside Delhi Police’s crowd-control machinery
Article Text:
Data for the first eight months of 2026 shows police handled more dharnas, processions, marches and strikes than during the corresponding period last year.





NEW DELHI: Delhi’s streets have seen a steady churn of protests, processions, marches, rallies and strikes this year, keeping police on their toes. Each programme brings its own set of crowd-control, traffic and law-and-order challenges.Data for the first eight months of 2026 shows police handled more dharnas, processions, marches and strikes than during the corresponding period last year. The number of dharnas rose from 1,235 in 2025 to 1,306 this year, while processions increased more sharply, from 1,672 to 1,908. Marches and rallies went up from 273 to 304, and strikes from 207 to 232.Not every category, however, witnessed an increase. Protests and miscellaneous activities declined from 2,172 last year to 2,032 this year. Meetings fell from 1,104 to 914, while demonstrations recorded the sharpest drop, from 808 in 2025 to 279 this year. Cops said the reasons behind these programmes varied, with most linked to political, religious and other issues.Behind every such gathering is a detailed assessment by police. Rules prescribe designated venues according to the expected strength of a gathering: Jantar Mantar for programmes involving up to 1,000 people, Ramlila Maidan for crowds between 1,000 and 50,000, and Burari for gatherings expected to draw more than 50,000 participants.But the process begins well before protesters reach a venue. Police first liaise with organisers to establish the expected turnout, venue, timing and duration of the programme, the presence of prominent attendees and the agenda. These inputs are then used to assess the likely impact on traffic, VVIP movement and the overall law-and-order situation.The decision to permit or reject a demonstration, dharna or public meeting is taken after examining whether it could obstruct traffic, pose a threat to public safety or disturb public tranquillity, police said.For protests at Jantar Mantar, the rules are particularly clear. “No march towards sensitive places from Jantar Mantar is allowed. Organiser(s) shall ensure that the protesters or demonstrators congregate as well as disperse peacefully from the identified spot only,” police said.The planning becomes more elaborate when protesters arrive from outside Delhi. Police coordinate with their counterparts in other states and remain in touch with organisers to gather details about the participants, timing, venue and nature of the programme. Once the inputs are collated, deployment is planned accordingly. Other district police units and traffic police are roped in, while arrangements are made for mobilisation of personnel, detention of protesters in case of law-and-order violations and food and water for the force deployed on the ground.Planned programmes such as marches, dharnas and protests can be challenging, but unplanned gatherings pose a bigger problem for police. Officers regularly monitor social media to check whether any calls for protests have been issued and try to prevent protesters from reaching restricted or sensitive areas. There is also the possibility of a gathering turning violent, in which case legal action is taken, police said.“At every sensitive place, there is deployment of forces and companies are kept nearby as a contingency. If protesters move towards a sensitive area, additional personnel can be mobilised,” an officer said.At the protest site, the job is not limited to managing the crowd. Police keep a close watch to prevent protesters from entering restricted areas or putting themselves or others at risk. Officers also track developments in other states and countries, particularly when there is a possibility of protests outside embassies or state bhavans.
Article Summary: Data for the first eight months of 2026 shows police handled more dharnas, processions, marches and strikes than during the corresponding period last year. The number of dharn as rose from 1,235 in 2025 to 1,306 this year, while processions increased more sharply. Marches and rallies went up from 273 to 304, and strikes from 207 to 232. Protests and miscellaneous activities declined from 2,172 last year to 2,032 this year.

Article Title: ‘Mad Sandhu’ murder: How a Punjab Police tip-off led to accused’s arrest in Ahmedabad
Article Text:
Police said he will be handed over to Punjab Police for further investigation and legal proceedings.





AHMEDABAD: The city crime branch on Wednesday arrested a key accused in the murder of Punjab-based social media influencer ‘Mad Sandhu’. Based on an input shared by Amritsar police, the accused, Parminder Prasad alias Parminder Kaka, was traced to the city’s Vadaj area.He had allegedly fired at Sandhu and had arranged the motorcycle used in the murder, investigators said.Sandhu, also known as Madhusudan Sandhu, was shot dead on Oct 3 on Loharka Road in Amritsar. According to police, two men riding a motorcycle approached him when he had gone to collect his car from a service centre and opened fire before fleeing. Sandhu died on the way to the hospital.An FIR was registered at Amritsar’s Cantonment police station under Section 103 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.A social media account associated with Goldy Dhillon allegedly claimed responsibility for the murder after the attack. Police are probing the suspected involvement of members of the gang in the killing.According to investigators, Parminder was the one who carried out the firing and arranged the motorcycle on which he arrived with the other assailant. After the murder, Parminder allegedly fled Punjab and reached Ahmedabad in an attempt to evade arrest.Crime branch officials said Amritsar Police shared information about Parminder’s involvement and his possible presence in Ahmedabad. “Parminder Prasad was fleeing to Mumbai and had broken his journey in Ahmedabad. He was arrested from Vadaj,” crime branch sources said.Officers are questioning Parminder to establish his movements after the murder, identify others involved in the killing and ascertain how he reached Ahmedabad. His mobile phone, travel details and contacts will also be examined.Police said he will be handed over to Punjab Police for further investigation and legal proceedings.The murder had drawn attention because Sandhu was a known social media personality, makeup artist and fashion designer. He was also associated with the LGBTQ community and had a substantial following on social media.
Article Summary: Parminder Prasad alias Parminder Kaka was traced to the city’s Vadaj area. He had allegedly fired at Sandhu and had arranged the motorcycle used in the murder. Sandhu, also known as Madhusudan Sandhu was shot dead on Oct 3 on Loharka Road in Amritsar.

Article Title: ‘Extraordinary measure rendered ordinary’: Madhya Pradesh High Court slams ‘reckless’ NSA use
Article Text:
Representative image





BHOPAL: Madhya Pradesh High Court has criticised the “reckless invocation” of the National Security Act (NSA), while quashing the preventive detention of two brothers under the law and warning that an extraordinary constitutional measure was being treated as an ordinary course of proceedings.A division bench headed by Justice Vivek Agarwal ordered the release of Rajendra Thakur and Rajesh Thakur, ruling that authorities failed to establish the requisite grounds for preventive detention and appeared to have acted without applying their minds. The Jabalpur district collector had ordered their detention on Jan 6 for three months over an alleged threat to public order, later extending the period.“Preventive detention, conceived as an extraordinary measure by the framers of our Constitution, has been rendered ordinary with its reckless invocation over the years as if it were available for use even in the ordinary course of proceedings,” HC said.The order, delivered on Sept 11, was made public on Oct 5.The court found that the brothers, named in 14 cases, had been acquitted in 11 when NSA was invoked against them. “This leads to a conclusion that correct facts were not placed before the competent authority, and that clearly suffers from the vice of non-application of mind,” the bench said.It added that authorities could have verified their criminal records with minimal effort through the Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems.The three pending cases against the duo pertained to obscene act, causing hurt and wrongful confinement, and throwing a crude bomb to create unrest.The bench was also alarmed that the proposal by the city SP to invoke NSA and the collector’s detention order passed through four officials and were completed on the same day.“Turning our attention to section 3(1) of the NSA, the govt has to arrive at a subjective satisfaction that a goonda (as in the present case) has to be detained, in order to prevent him from acting in a manner prejudicial to the maintenance of public order. The application of mind to invoke the aforesaid extraordinary measure appears to be missing in the present case,” the HC said.“There is no requisite satisfaction recorded by the detaining authority that the detenus are a threat to public order. It also appears that the haste with which the matter was processed in a single day took away independent exercise of mind by the detaining authority,” it added.Citing the Supreme Court’s 2023 ruling in Ameena Begum vs State of Telangana, the bench stressed that constitutional safeguards must be enforced to prevent arbitrary detention.“To unchain the shackles of preventive detention, it is important that safeguards enshrined in our Constitution, particularly under the ‘golden triangle’ formed by Articles 14, 19 and 21, are diligently enforced,” the court said.The ruling comes amid similar judicial criticism of NSA detentions in Uttar Pradesh. Last month, Allahabad HC ordered the release of Delhi University graduate Aakriti Choudhary, detained in connection with a workers’ protest in April, and imposed a fine of Rs 5 lakh on Noida DM and other officials.In its Sept 2 order, Allahabad HC rebuked UP’s administrative machinery for invoking NSA without applying its mind or relying on credible evidence. It stressed that preventive detention was an exception, not a substitute for ordinary criminal law.Reminding police and administrative officials that their allegiance was to the Constitution, not the political executive, Allahabad HC warned that an errant bureaucracy could reduce UP to an Orwellian dystopia.
Article Summary: Madhya Pradesh High Court criticises the “reckless invocation” of the National Security Act (NSA) The court quashes the preventive detention of two brothers under the law. The brothers, named in 14 cases, had been acquitted in 11 when NSA was invoked against them.

Article Title: Delhi shuts liquor stores on October 9, 10 ahead of CJP protest
Article Text:
While the retail liquor stores will be closed, the sale of liquor will continue to operate normally from licensed restaurants, bars and clubs, clarified an official.





NEW DELHI: All liquor stores in the whole of the city limits will be closed on Oct 9 and 10 in the wake of planned protests called by Cockroach Janta Party and others on Oct 10 against alleged irregularities in SIR and in support of their call and demands to seek the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.“In view of the prevailing situation and inputs received from Delhi Police , as a preventive measure aimed at maintaining public order, it is hereby ordered that all retail liquor vends with licenses in Form L6, L6& L6FG, L8, L10 and L8 & L14 operating in Delhi will be completely closed on 09.10.2026 and 10.10.2026,” a circular dated Oct 8 issued by the excise department stated.L-6 licences are issued for retail sale of Indian liquor through authorised vends, while L-6FG relates to retail sale of foreign liquor.L-8 licences cover retail sale of country liquor while L-10 is associated with retail sale of liquor from outlets located inside malls and L-14 licence is for sale of beer from country liquor outlets.While the retail liquor stores will be closed, the sale of liquor will continue to operate normally from licensed restaurants, bars and clubs, clarified an official.“The closure of all retail liquor stores is a preemptive move to prevent any disruption to public order. The stores in whole of Delhi have been closed because Delhi is a city state that is why localised closure of liquor stores may not serve the purpose fully,” said an official.
Article Summary: All liquor stores in the whole of the city limits will be closed on Oct 9 and 10. Cockroach Janta Party and others on Oct 10 against alleged irregularities in SIR. L-6 licences are issued for retail sale of Indian liquor through authorised vends.

Article Title: Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar claims plot to trap him in sting operation
Article Text:
Deputy CM G Parameshwara and home minister Priyank Kharge backed Shivakumar’s claims.

DKS puts his colleagues, officials on

honey-trap alert

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your opinion on the influence of external agencies in political smear campaigns? It’s a significant issue that needs regulation. It’s overblown and doesn’t happen often. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





BENGALURU: Chief minister DK Shivakumar Thursday claimed an attempt was made to trap him in a sting operation soon after he took charge, saying he had photographs and documents to identify those behind it.His claim came a day after Union minister HD Kumaraswamy alleged that Shivakumar had used a sting operation to force Siddaramaiah out as chief minister.“I have collected details of the people through our police officers and have the documentation ready. I know the pretext under which they came and whom they met,” Shivakumar said.He said it was not the first such attempt, recalling that a private television channel had earlier tried something similar when he was minister.Shivakumar cautioned cabinet colleagues and govt officials to remain vigilant. He said he had three rings of security around him and had moved several people out of their positions over what he described as questionable intent. “Some of these people were hired by political functionaries, and I have strong evidence,” he said.Deputy CM G Parameshwara and home minister Priyank Kharge backed Shivakumar’s claims.PWD minister Satish Jarkiholi said people from North India, allegedly linked to a private agency, had tried to trap the CM. “When rasgulla, Maddur vada and Mulbagal dosa are served, one ought to be careful. Such things are natural in politics,” he said.BJP state president BY Vijayendra hit back, saying Congress had a history of such operations. He cited the case of BJP MLA Ramesh Jarkiholi, who was allegedly honey-trapped.
Article Summary: Chief minister DK Shivakumar claims an attempt was made to trap him in a sting operation soon after he took charge. He said he had photographs and documents to identify those behind it. His claim came a day after Union minister HD Kumaraswamy alleged that Shivak Kumar had used a sting operations to force Siddaramaiah out as chief minister.

Article Title: 7 killed, over 20 injured in truck-pickup collision in Gujarat
Article Text:
The injured were taken to hospital for treatment (AI Image)

(With agency inputs)





AHMEDABAD: At least seven workers were killed and more than 20 others injured after a truck collided head-on with a pickup truck at a renewable energy park near Khavda in Gujarat’s Kutch district in the early hours of Friday, police said.The accident occurred between 3am and 4am inside the park, they said.“A truck and a Bolero Camper (pickup truck) travelling in opposite directions collided. The impact left the pickup truck mangled,” said sub-inspector MB Chavda from Khavda police station told news agency PTI.The official said all the victims were travelling in the pickup truck.“Seven workers were trapped inside the wrecked Bolero Camper. They were taken out with the help of a crane. While all of them died, over 20 injured workers were sent to the hospital in an ambulance,” he said.An investigation has been launched, and police are looking into potential negligence that caused the tragedy at the sprawling clean energy installation, he added.
Article Summary: A truck collided head-on with a pickup truck at a renewable energy park near Khavda in Gujarat’s Kutch district. The accident occurred between 3am and 4am inside the park. Police are looking into potential negligence that caused the tragedy.

Article Title: 39% Mumbadevi voters out of draft roll, alleges Congress MLA Amin Patel
Article Text:
Patel has represented Mumbadevi, a mixed-population constituency that includes Dongri, Nagpada and Kamathipura, since 2009. (File photo)





MUMBAI: Nearly 40% of Mumbadevi assembly constituency’s voters have been categorised as permanently shifted, dead, untraceable/absent, duplicate and ‘other reasons’ during SIR, local Congress MLA Amin Patel has alleged.Patel said that several voters had been wrongly placed in these categories and wrote to Maharashtra chief electoral officer S Chockalingam, urging him to ensure that no voter was marked in any of the five categories or otherwise excluded due to errors in data entry, processing or verification. He also questioned how information collected during SIR could be excluded from the draft roll and listed several voters “wrongly left out”. “Forms have been accepted from people, yet they have been marked as dead. There are so many such cases. In some places, people have been unable to find BLOs. Even where available, BLOs have no clarity on Form 6’s format following what SC said,” Patel said.Patel has represented Mumbadevi, a mixed-population constituency that includes Dongri, Nagpada and Kamathipura, since 2009. The seat is considered a Congress stronghold.In his letter, Patel said BLOs had visited voters and collected the prescribed forms and details, making it difficult to understand how some of the same voters were subsequently excluded from the draft roll. He urged election authorities not to remove voters without proper verification.Chockalingam said he had not seen Patel’s letter and maintained that such categorisation was not specific to Mumbai or Maharashtra, citing urban mobility as a major factor.“Urban mobility is common across the country, where around 40% of people are not found at their original place during address and related verification process. We put them under five different categories and their names are not there on the draft list. They have the option of filing Form 6 to get themselves included in the list,” he said.Form 6 has recently been at the centre of controversy after a CJI-led SC bench rejected the Election Commission’s claim that the court had upheld the declaration attached to the form, making it clear that it had not approved any modification to it.State electoral officials said they would accept Form 6 applications in accordance with the prescribed procedure and in view of the SC’s observations. Decisions on the applications will be taken in accordance with the final outcome of the court proceedings.In Maharashtra, the enumeration exercise has been completed and electoral officials have verified voter details. Officials said BLOs collected information and signatures from residents, while voters reported dead, shifted elsewhere, absent from their registered addresses or found to have duplicate entries in another area were excluded from the draft roll.Electoral officials said public representatives had also been asked to verify the published draft roll and flag missing or incorrect names.
Article Summary: Mumbadevi assembly constituency’s voters have been categorised as permanently shifted, dead, untraceable/absent, duplicate and ‘other reasons’ during SIR, local Congress MLA Amin Patel has alleged. Patel said that several voters had been wrongly placed in these categories and wrote to Maharashtra chief electoral officer S Chockalingam.

Article Title: NR Congress candidate Ashok Anand wins Thattanchavady bypoll in Puducherry by 8,500 votes
Article Text:
The win consolidates the party's influence in the region as local leadership expressed gratitude to the voters of Thattanchavady for their mandate.





PUDUCHERRY: In a significant electoral development, N R Congress candidate Ashok Anand has secured a decisive victory in the Thattanchavady assembly constituency by-election in Puducherry.He polled 13,358 votes as against his nearest rival candidate E Vinayagam of Congress who polled 4,876 votes and won by a margin of 8,482 votes.Barring Vinayagam, other candidates including K Sethu Selvam (2,664) of DMK lost their deposits.The victory was formally announced following the conclusion of the vote-counting process.The by-election witnessed a high-stakes contest among key political forces in the Union territory.The Congress party candidate contested with the support of TVK (Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam).AINRC supporters gathered in large numbers to celebrate the victory, waving party flags and shouting slogans in support of Anand and N R Congress.The win consolidates the party's influence in the region as local leadership expressed gratitude to the voters of Thattanchavady for their mandate.
Article Summary: N R Congress candidate Ashok Anand has secured a decisive victory in the Thattanchavady assembly constituency by-election in Puducherry. He polled 13,358 votes as against his nearest rival candidate E Vinayagam of Congress who polled 4,876 votes and won by a margin of 8,482 votes.

Article Title: Lucknow double murder: Home Guard personnel kills wife, daughter with mobile charging cable; informs police
Article Text:
The accused, identified as Ravindra Shankar Gupta

Elder daughter files complaint





LUCKNOW: A 56-year-old Home Guard personnel allegedly strangled his wife and 32-year-old daughter to death using a mobile phone charging cable at their residence in the Bhola Kheda locality of Krishna Nagar in Lucknow on Friday morning.The accused, identified as Ravindra Shankar Gupta, informed the police about the murders himself, following which a police team reached the spot and took him into custody.The deceased have been identified as Shyam Dulari (55) and her daughter, Pooja Sahu (32).The incident took place in a lane near Gauri Studio, triggering panic in the neighbourhood.According to police, Gupta told investigators that he was frustrated with his daughter's personal life. He said that she had gone through two failed marriages and was now in a relationship with another man.His wife, however, was supportive of their daughter, a factor that reportedly contributed to tensions within the family.Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) Mohammad Mustaq said Gupta, a resident of Bhola Kheda, had informed the police himself about the deaths of his wife and daughter. A team reached the house, collected evidence and initiated an investigation.Police said a case was being registered based on a complaint lodged by the couple's elder daughter. Both bodies were sent for post-mortem examinations to establish the exact cause of death and gather further evidence.Investigators are examining the circumstances leading to the killings and verifying the accused's account of the family dispute. Police said further investigation was underway.
Article Summary: Ravindra Shankar Gupta, 56, allegedly strangled his wife and 32-year-old daughter to death using a mobile phone charging cable at their residence in Lucknow. The incident triggered panic in the neighbourhood. Gupta told investigators that he was frustrated with his daughter's personal life.

Article Title: CJP protest: What’s open and what’s closed in Delhi on October 10
Article Text:
CJP protest scheduled for October 10

What will be closed

1. All retail liquor stores

2. Several Mail and Express trains

3. Entry and exit gates at 57 Metro stations may be closed

What will remain open

1. Licensed restaurants, bars and clubs

2. Other regular services

Police step up security ahead of protests





NEW DELHI: Delhi will see restrictions on retail liquor sales and cancellations of several Mail and Express trains on October 10 amid planned protests by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), Left groups and student outfits of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The protests are also aimed at seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Police have stepped up security and outreach efforts across the city, urging residents, students and young people to avoid activities that could disrupt public order.Here is a look at what will remain open and what will be closed in Delhi on October 10.All retail liquor outlets across Delhi will remain closed on October 9 and 10 following an order issued by the excise department on October 8.The closure applies to retail liquor vends operating under specified licence categories, including outlets selling Indian liquor, foreign liquor and country liquor, as well as certain outlets in malls.The excise department said the decision was taken as a preventive measure to maintain public order in view of the prevailing situation and inputs received from Delhi Police.However, liquor sales at licensed restaurants, bars and clubs will continue as usual, an official clarified.Indian Railways has ordered the cancellation of several Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4am and 2pm on October 10.According to a railway order issued on October 9, trains departing from their originating stations after 2pm on October 9 and scheduled to reach either of the two stations during the specified period on October 10 will be cancelled at source.The decision was taken due to the possibility of severe road traffic congestion around the two railway stations. Railway officials have not confirmed whether the cancellations are directly linked to the planned protests.Delhi Police have asked DMRC to close entry and exit gates at 57 Metro stations from 9pm on October 9 and continue the restrictions on October 10 until the situation normalises. Train frequency at these stations may also be reduced in view of the proposed protests at Jantar Mantar and other locations. Passengers are advised to check DMRC updates before travelling.While retail liquor shops will remain shut, licensed restaurants, bars and clubs in Delhi will continue to serve liquor as usual, according to an excise department official.No blanket closure of other regular public services or commercial establishments has been announced in the information available. Residents should check for specific advisories before travelling or making plans.Delhi Police have warned against the proposed CJP protest on October 10, stating that Section 163 is in force in the national capital and any gathering in violation of the restrictions would be considered illegal.Police teams have contacted market welfare associations, resident welfare associations and Aman committees in several areas, asking them to counsel people against participating in activities that could disturb public order.Sources said police were also checking hotels for last-minute bookings and monitoring railway stations and other transit points. Officers were approaching groups gathered at these locations to inquire about their plans.The protests have been called over alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise, with demonstrators also demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
Article Summary: All retail liquor outlets across Delhi will remain closed on October 9 and 10. Several Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations will be cancelled. Entry and exit gates at 57 Metro stations may be closed. Police have stepped up security and outreach efforts.

Article Title: 'Youth are no longer scared of you, PM Modi': CJP’s Abhijeet Dipke
Article Text:
“I’ll be landing in Delhi tomorrow and will march to Jantar Mantar, come what may,” Dipke tweeted.

Delhi Police

warns against CJP protest on October 10

Dipke shares Bengaluru visit, thanks

Prakash Raj

(With agency inputs)





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leader Abhijeet Dipke on Friday said he would march to Delhi’s Jantar Mantar on October 10, despite police restrictions on the proposed protest.In a post on X, Dipke alleged that thousands of youngsters had been detained across the country ahead of the demonstration and accused the BJP government of trying to intimidate protesters.“Thousands of youngsters have been detained across country by the BJP Govt ahead of our October 10 protest.“This intimidation is not going to work, Modi. The youth of this country are no longer scared of you.“I’ll be landing in Delhi tomorrow and will march to Jantar Mantar, come what may,” Dipke tweeted.The statement came amid Delhi Police’s warning against the proposed CJP protest, with the force saying that prohibitory restrictions under Section 163 were in force in the national capital and that unauthorised gatherings would invite legal action.Deputy commissioner of police (DCP) Shrishti Pandey said protests were not permitted at Jantar Mantar or any other location while the restrictions remained in force.“Section 163 is in effect, meaning protests are not permitted—neither at Jantar Mantar nor anywhere else. Any gathering will be considered illegal, and we would be compelled to take necessary legal action against it,” Pandey told news agency ANI.The DCP also urged people not to take part in the proposed demonstration, asking them to prioritise their safety and that of their families.“I would like to urge the protestors not to participate in such illegal gatherings. Please prioritise your own safety as well. Also, consider the safety of your family,” she said.Earlier on Friday, Dipke shared a separate post about his recent visit to Bengaluru, thanking those who had welcomed him during his stay.“Leaving Bengaluru with so much love in my heart. The warmth, affection and kindness I’ve received over the last two days have been truly overwhelming,” he wrote.Dipke also thanked Kavitha Lankesh and Esha Lankesh, referring to them as his “new family”, and said he hoped to return to the city.He expressed gratitude to actor Prakash Raj and his “elder sister” Aafreen Nawaz for inviting him to Bengaluru and introducing him to the city’s warmth and generosity.“You’ve all given me more than just beautiful memories. You’ve given me a home to return to,” he added.
Article Summary: “I’ll be landing in Delhi tomorrow and will march to Jantar Mantar, come what may,” Dipke tweeted. The statement came amid Delhi Police’s warning against the proposed CJP protest. The force said that prohibitory restrictions under Section 163 were in force.

Article Title: ‘40 cops in civil dress': CJP alleges Deepak Baliyan placed under house arrest ahead of protest
Article Text:
The party also raised concerns over the proposed closure of metro stations and train cancellations ahead of its October 10 protest in Delhi

Delhi Police proposes closure of 57 metro stations

CJP protest planned for October 10





NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) on Friday alleged that its national organisation co-in-charge, Deepak Baliyan, had been placed under house arrest, claiming that around 40 police personnel in plain clothes were present at his residence.In a post on X, the CJP alleged that Alwar Police had returned to Baliyan’s residence after detaining him from his home at night. The party also shared his concerns about the safety of his family.“My family is scared and fears for their safety. Alwar Police will be solely responsible if anything happens to any member of my family,” the post quoted Baliyan as saying.The party also raised concerns over the proposed closure of metro stations and train cancellations ahead of its October 10 protest in Delhi, asking whether the country was witnessing “the making of an Emergency”.In a separate post, the CJP alleged that the government was rattled by the planned demonstration and listed the possible restrictions on public transport in the national capital.“Modi Govt is SHOOK to its core,” the party said, claiming that 57 metro stations could remain closed in Delhi on Saturday, all trains to New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin stations between 4am and 2pm could be cancelled, and more than 30,000 police personnel could be deployed across the city.“Are we witnessing the making of an Emergency?” the party asked.The allegations come ahead of the CJP’s proposed protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10 against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Meanwhile, Delhi Police has requested the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) to close 57 metro stations from 9pm on Friday until Saturday, citing the likelihood of “unruly mob movement towards sensitive locations”.In a letter dated Thursday, Joint Commissioner of Police (Transport Range) Rajneesh Gupta said the frequency of metro trains passing through the identified stations could also be reduced on October 10, depending on the situation.The proposed measures are intended to address security concerns around the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar and other locations in the national capital.The stations listed in the police request include Janpath, Patel Chowk, Central Secretariat, Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, Barakhamba Road, Supreme Court, Indraprastha, Kashmere Gate, Chandni Chowk, INA, Hauz Khas, Azadpur, Jamia Millia Islamia, Shaheen Bagh, Welcome and Rohini West.The proposed closures and service changes would affect commuters travelling through several parts of Delhi. The police request, however, does not by itself confirm that the DMRC has implemented the measures.The CJP has announced a youth-led demonstration at Jantar Mantar on October 10 over alleged “vote theft”, the exclusion of young voters from electoral rolls and other concerns related to the Election Commission.Delhi Police has warned against the proposed gathering, saying prohibitory restrictions under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) are in force in the national capital. Police have said unauthorised gatherings would invite legal action.CJP leaders, however, have maintained that they intend to proceed with the protest despite the restrictions.
Article Summary: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) on Friday alleged that its national organisation co-in-charge, Deepak Baliyan, was under house arrest. The party also raised concerns over the proposed closure of metro stations and train cancellations ahead of its October 10 protest in Delhi. Delhi Police has requested the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) to close 57 metro stations from 9pm on Friday until Saturday.

Article Title: ‘Delhi bandh tomorrow’: CJP’s Saurav Das takes swipe at Delhi Police
Article Text:
Police denied permission for the CJP’s Oct 10 protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar, a senior officer said.

Delhi Police Seeks Metro Restrictions At 57 Stations

Police Deny Permission For

October 10 Protest

(With agency inputs)





NEW DELHI: “The Government of India has called for a Delhi Bandh tomorrow. Hilarious!” Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Saurav Das said on Friday, taking a swipe at the Delhi Police ’s request to consider closing the entry and exit gates of 57 metro stations ahead of proposed protests on October 10.In another post, Das alleged that trains arriving in Delhi had been cancelled, questioning how long the authorities could continue imposing such restrictions.“The Emperor is so scared that he has cancelled trains coming to Delhi tomorrow! But for how many days can they do this?” Das wrote on X.Referring to the Covid-19 lockdown and the hardships faced by migrant workers, Das said people would find ways to convey their message to the government.“A nation awakened will find all ways to convey its message. Remember how you forced migrants all over the country to walk hundreds of kilometres during Covid?
