The same people will do it again, to teach those in government a lesson,” he added.Delhi Police on Friday requested the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) to consider closing the entry and exit gates of 57 metro stations from 9pm on October 9 in view of proposed protests at Jantar Mantar and other locations in the New Delhi district on October 10.In a letter dated October 8, police cited the possibility of unruly crowd movement towards sensitive locations. The communication also proposed reducing the frequency of metro trains passing through the identified stations.The proposed restrictions would remain in force on October 10 until the situation returned to normal.The stations listed in the communication span several metro corridors and include Rajiv Chowk, Central Secretariat, Patel Chowk, Janpath, Mandi House, Supreme Court, New Delhi, Kashmere Gate, Jama Masjid, Chawri Bazar, Karol Bagh, Vishwavidyalaya, Hauz Khas, INA, Lajpat Nagar, Sarai Kale Khan-Nizamuddin, Jamia Millia Islamia, Okhla Vihar, Rithala, Rohini East, Rohini West, Shahdara, Welcome and Maujpur, among others.The list also includes Inderlok, Seelampur, Jafrabad, Yamuna Vihar, Azadpur, Majlis Park and Haiderpur Badli Mor.Delhi Police has denied permission for a protest called by the CJP and some student organisations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar on October 10, a senior police officer told news agency PTI on Friday.Police cited the late submission of the application and alleged rule violations during a previous demonstration as reasons for denying permission.Joint commissioner of police, New Delhi range, Nupur Prasad, said police received the application on October 7, just three days before the proposed protest.According to the rules, applications for such demonstrations must be submitted at least 10 days in advance, she said.Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which empowers authorities to issue orders to prevent potential disturbances, has also been imposed in the New Delhi district, Prasad said.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Saurav Das takes a swipe at Delhi Police. Police denied permission for the CJP’s Oct 10 protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar, a senior officer said.

Article Title: California is set to become the first US state to ban popular kitchen countertops made with engineered stone, Australia did the same in 2024; 'fear' is growing ...
Article Text:
Disclaimer: It's an AI-generated image used for representative purpose only

Why California wants to ban countertops made of engineered stones

California’s petition wants to follow Australian model

America's third-largest state California is reportedly on track to enact the country's first ban on engineered quartz countertops. According to a report in USA Today, the upcoming ban is in response to an alarming rise in Silicosis, a debilitating lung disease, in people who work with the material. Over the past decade, engineered quartz has reportedly dominated American kitchen and bathroom renovations, as it is an affordable, durable, and low-maintenance alternative to natural marble and granite. However, that commercial boom has coincided with an occupational health crisis. Australia enacted a nationwide complete ban on engineered stones in 2024.Engineered stones, also called artificial stone or quartz countertops, are man-made stone countertops designed to look like natural stone. According to data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), engineered stone is manufactured by binding 90% to 95% crushed quartz with resins, polymers, and pigments. When workers cut, grind, drill, sand, or polish these slabs, the process generates high concentrations of respirable crystalline silica dust. Inhaling these microscopic particles causes progressive, irreversible scarring of lung tissue.California has emerged as an epicenter of the crisis, home to a large concentration of fabrication shops and an escalating caseload among stone cutters. The state, where several quartz countertop manufacturers and fabricators are based, has seen a notable rise in cases of lung diseases.In a recent report, the California Department of Public Health estimated that 662 silicosis cases, including 35 deaths and 75 cases resulting in lung transplants, have been diagnosed among quartz manufacturers and workers in the state since 2019. In the petition, the California Division of Occupational Safety and Health, or Cal/OSHA, called the cluster of silicosis cases a "crisis." It said, "California is experiencing a rapidly worsening silicosis crisis among artificial stone workers, driven by dangerous materials and regulatory shortcomings. "The petition also mentions Australia banning these engineered stones. It said, "Australia faced a comparable crisis and, after finding that enforcement alone was ineffective, implemented a nationwide prohibition of artificial stone containing more than 1% crystalline silica in July 2024. The ban succeeded: safer alternatives replaced artificial stone without reported job losses or significant consumer impact, and enforcement became dramatically simpler. Prohibiting fabrication and installation of artificial stone in California could substantially mitigate silicosis risk while simplifying enforcement. There is, however, an important caveat — Australia controls the entire supply chain (imports, manufacture, and sale), whereas Cal/OSHA can only regulate sites of employment (such as locations where fabrication and installation occurs). If artificial stone remains commercially available in California, some non-compliant shops may go underground, concentrating risk in the least regulated settings."
Article Summary: Engineered stones, also called artificial stone or quartz countertops, are man- made stone countertops designed to look like natural stone. Inhaling these microscopic particles causes progressive, irreversible scarring of lung tissue. Australia enacted a nationwide complete ban on engineered stones in 2024.

Article Title: US suspends Microsoft from Green Card sponsorship programme; company responds: Microsoft only files H-1B petitions for those who...
Article Text:
Microsoft suspended from US Green Card sponsorship programme as JD Vance alleges H-1B abuse. (AP Photo/Thibault Camus, File)

A Vance-led fraud probe is behind Microsoft's PERM suspension

Microsoft says most of its H-1B filings were for existing employees

Vance says the Microsoft suspension will last "as long as it needs to"

The US government has suspended Microsoft from the Permanent Labor Certification Program (PERM), the process most employers must clear before sponsoring a foreign worker for a Green Card. Vice President JD Vance and Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling announced the move at a press conference in Washington on October 8, and the Labor Department will now neither accept new PERM applications from Microsoft nor process the ones already pending.Vance singled out the company as the worst offender. "There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused the system more than Microsoft," he said, claiming Microsoft laid off around 6,000 American workers last year while employing 6,300 people on H-1B visas and securing nearly 3,000 Green Cards. Microsoft has pushed back, saying the vast majority of its US employees are Americans.The suspension follows an investigation by an anti-fraud task force that Vance chairs. Officials argued that PERM is meant for roles needing "hyper-specialized" skills that are hard to find in the US, and accused Microsoft of misrepresenting its needs to replace American staff with cheaper foreign hires."The H-1B visa is how the people get into the United States in the first place, and then a PERM program is how those employees stay," Vance said.He also claimed that for every worker Microsoft laid off, it brought in "one and a half foreign indentured servants." Sonderling said Microsoft was suspended "due to multiple active federal investigations."Microsoft is the largest filer of PERM applications, according to Labor Department data, so the freeze puts a sizeable pipeline of employee Green Card cases on hold.Microsoft responded with a blog post on Thursday. It said about 80% of the roughly 6,000 H-1B applications it filed in the last fiscal year were to extend or change the status of existing employees, not to hire new people. The rest were for people already living legally in the US, and they make up only 1% of its US workforce."Microsoft only files H-1B petitions for those who meet the rigorous standards of this visa category," the company said. It added that its H-1B wages are among the highest of all filings, and that these employees are paid the same as anyone else doing comparable work.Data from Levels.fyi places Microsoft fourth among H-1B sponsors this year, with 21,706 petitions at a median base salary of $180,710. The company also said in July it would cut 4,800 jobs, or about 2.1% of its global workforce.Vance did not spell out what Microsoft must do to regain access to the programme. "Our message to Microsoft is not that we want to harm your company, it's that we want your company to thrive, but we want it to thrive by employing and empowering your fellow Americans," he said.The timing stood out. Hours later, President Donald Trump was due to present Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella with the National Medal of Technology and Innovation, the country's highest honour for tech achievement. Just over a week earlier, India-born Nadella, who joined Microsoft in 1992, sat two seats from Vance at a White House luncheon on AI.The move extends a wider crackdown on skilled-worker visas ahead of the November midterms, which last September brought a one-time $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions. For Microsoft employees already in the queue, the wait was long to begin with: PERM applications took an average of 336 days to process in August. Now it has no end date at all.
Article Summary: Microsoft suspended from US Green Card sponsorship programme as JD Vance alleges H-1B abuse. Vance-led fraud probe is behind Microsoft's PERM suspension. Microsoft has pushed back, saying the vast majority of its US employees are Americans. Microsoft is the largest filer of PERM applications, according to Labor Department data.

Article Title: Dario Amodei wants to make sure it gets both Democrats and Republicans on its side as it hires ...
Article Text:
Why it matters

Experts divided on how unusual it is

Calls for transparency

Anthropic's political footprint

OpenAI's different approach

Dario Amodei's Anthropic is building a dedicated political engagement operation ahead of the 2028 US presidential election, highlighting how crucial government relationships and AI policy debates have become for the rapidly growing artificial intelligence industry. As reported by Fortune, Anthropic is creating a "presidential engagement" programme that will work directly with Republican and Democratic presidential candidates on AI-related issues, help shape the company's political strategy and oversee its political funding activities. The company is currently hiring a Political Programs Lead to spearhead the initiative. “Most companies hire people with Democratic and Republican backgrounds for a reason—the campaigns trust people who come from their party and understand how they work,” said the company. The role will be responsible for building and managing Anthropic's presidential engagement programme for the 2028 election cycle, educating candidates and their advisers about AI policy, preparing company executives for discussions with campaigns and planning for party conventions and presidential transitions."Decisions made over the next two years will shape the future enormously," the job description states."We want every serious candidate and elected official, in both parties, to understand the technology and the case for governing it well."The program is taking shape before the November midterms and an impending IPO that could value Anthropic at up to $2 trillion. Fortune said it underscores how central government policy, and White House support in particular, have become to the AI industry.Anthropic's relationship with the Trump administration has been rocky. In March, the Department of Defense designated the company a "supply chain risk" after a clash over how the military could use its technology. CEO Dario Amodei has called for slowing AI development to shore up safeguards and has advocated government regulation, a view President Trump rejects, citing the race with China. Last week, Amodei attended a White House event with other AI CEOs and signed an accord committing to self-regulation.Lobbying by tech companies is standard, and OpenAI is hiring a U.S. Congressional Lead to advance its legislative priorities. But some experts said a formal, dedicated presidential program is different. Bruce F. Freed, president of the nonpartisan Center for Political Accountability, said companies usually deal with campaigns through government affairs staff. He had not seen such formalized engagement through a presidential election engagement committee. "My reading is this is an AI company effort aimed at shaping or staving off government regulation or oversight," he said.Katie Harbath, founder and CEO of the tech policy firm Anchor Change and a former Facebook public policy director, did not find it unusual. The role sounded like her old job, she said, and like what many companies have. What stood out to her was that it includes running PAC money, which is usually a separate function. She described it as the start of building relationships with whoever is in the White House in 2029.Harbath also said earning trust across both parties could be hard, because campaigns tend to trust people from their own side. She expects the job to be challenging and high-pressure.Sen. Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) said the job search is a reminder that frontier AI companies are building political operations alongside their products. Companies have a right to take part in democracy and educate policymakers, he said, but "education and influence are not the same thing." He urged Anthropic to share more about the program and said AI rules should be set by accountable elected representatives, not "by whichever company has the best-resourced political program. "The job description calls Anthropic "equal parts research lab, policy think tank, and technology company" and stresses that its political participation is bipartisan. The role also includes running "the day-to-day of Anthropic's political giving" and helping employees who choose to take part in politics do so "in an informed way."In April, Anthropic set up its first employee-funded PAC, AnthroPAC, which lets employees give up to $5,000 a year, the legal cap. Other tech companies have similar PACs, such as MetaPAC and AmazonPAC. Individuals can give far more outside PAC limits, and the IPO will likely deepen employees' pockets. Politico reported that Amodei gave $1 million in July to Public First, a super PAC that favors AI regulation. Other employees have given hundreds of thousands of dollars to that group and other advocacy organizations.OpenAI has no employee-funded PACs, a policy it highlighted in a June 2026 blog post. Its leaders have instead made personal donations and sought favor with the Trump administration. CEO Sam Altman gave $1 million to Trump's 2024 inauguration fund. President Greg Brockman gave $25 million to the pro-AI super PAC Leading the Future, then canceled a second planned $25 million donation after employee backlash, including employees setting up a rival super PAC for stricter AI safety laws.Sarah E. Kreps, director of Cornell University's Tech Policy Institute, said AI is already a big issue in 2026 and will become more prominent in 2028, moving from the abstract to concerns such as jobs, data centers and privacy.
Article Summary: Anthropic is building a dedicated political engagement operation ahead of the 2028 US presidential election. The company is currently hiring a Political Programs Lead to spearhead the initiative. The job description calls Anthropic "equal parts research lab, policy think tank, and technology company"

Article Title: Japan protests Russia’s bid to extradite ICC top judge Tomoko Akane, a Japanese national, over Putin arrest warrant
Article Text: Japan on Friday lodged a formal protest against Russia’s request for the extradition of International Criminal Court (ICC) President Tomoko Akane, a Japanese national, from the Netherlands, describing the move as “unacceptable. ”The protest came a day after Russia’s Prosecutor General’s Office submitted extradition requests to the Netherlands, where the ICC is headquartered in The Hague, and several other countries for Akane and nine other ICC staff members.“Measures targeting individuals connected to the ICC are unjust and unacceptable. We regret that Russia made extradition requests to multiple countries nevertheless,” Japan’s deputy chief cabinet secretary Masanao Ozaki told reporters, according to the Associated Press.Tokyo would consider further action, including additional formal protests, Ozaki added.The requests followed Moscow’s issuance of arrest warrants for Akane and eight others in response to the ICC’s 2023 warrant for Russian President Vladimir Putin over the war in Ukraine. The Moscow City Court last year sentenced all nine in absentia to prison terms.Russia has accused the ICC of violating fundamental principles and norms of international law by issuing arrest warrants against Russian citizens without evidence, according to state news agency TASS.Relations between Japan and Russia have deteriorated since Putin visited the Kuril Islands, a Pacific island chain claimed by both countries, in August, marking his first visit to the archipelago. The Soviet Union seized the islands from Japan in the final days of World War II, and the dispute has prevented them from signing a peace treaty formally ending hostilities.Japan has also sought to balance its support for the ICC with its close ties to the United States, which opposes the court. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has faced domestic criticism over this balancing act.“We have consistently supported the ICC and will continue to do so,” Takaichi told parliament on Friday.Washington has accused the ICC of exceeding its mandate and imposed sanctions on Akane and about a dozen other court officials in retaliation for investigations into Israeli officials over the war in Gaza and probes into the conduct of US military personnel in Afghanistan.The sanctions freeze any assets held in US jurisdictions by those targeted and bar the officials and their family members from entering the United States.
Article Summary: Japan lodged a formal protest against Russia’s request for the extradition of International Criminal Court (ICC) President Tomoko Akane, a Japanese national. The protest came a day after Russia submitted extradition requests to the Netherlands, where the ICC is headquartered in The Hague.

Article Title: 'Is Delhi Narendra Modi's property?': Abhijeet Dipke questions heavy police deployment, curbs ahead of Oct 10 protest
Article Text:
Dipke said CJP activists were ready to face detention or arrest over the proposed demonstration.

(With inputs from ANI)





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activist Abhijeet Dipke on Friday questioned the heavy police deployment and restrictions ahead of the organisation's proposed protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on October 10, asking whether the capital was the property of Prime Minister Narendra Modi or Union home minister Amit Shah Dipke asserted that the protest would be held despite the organisation not receiving permission from Delhi Police.He said the demonstration would go ahead regardless of whether permission was granted and said activists were prepared to face arrest.Questioning the measures taken ahead of the protest, Dipke said, "What is this fear? Why are you this scared? You are scared of the youth in the country. You shut down trains, you shut down metro, what should one do?"He also questioned the inconvenience caused to passengers, alleging that restrictions on public transport and roads would themselves cause hardship to ordinary people."Is Delhi a property of Narendra Modi or Amit Shah? Is this their ancestral property? Is this their paternal property? On one hand, you say that due to the protest, people are facing inconvenience, and on the other hand, you shut down all the metro, you shut down all the railways, you block all the roads. Now, won't there be inconvenience for people?" he said.Dipke said CJP activists were ready to face detention or arrest over the proposed demonstration."How many people will they detain? Arrest me, detain me! Saurabh is ready, Ashutosh is ready. Arrest me, detain me!" he said.Questioning the requirement for police permission, Dipke cited Article 19 of the Constitution and said Jantar Mantar was a designated protest site."Did Gyanesh Kumar take permission? Before deleting 13 crore votes, did Gyanesh Kumar take permission? The Supreme Court didn't even give approval for the Form 6 modification. So, when Gyanesh Kumar, without telling anyone, without asking anyone, deletes 13 crore votes, then to protest against him, the constitutional right we have according to Article 19, what is the need for permission?" he said.Dipke also questioned the Delhi Police's statement that applications for protests at Jantar Mantar must be submitted at least 10 days in advance, linking the restrictions to the proposed demonstration."The government is very serious. I think Narendra Modi and Amit Shah should keep checking their blood pressure. The kind of fear this government is showing," he said.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activist Abhijeet Dipke on Friday questioned the heavy police deployment and restrictions ahead of the organisation's proposed protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on October 10. Article Title: 'My entire family will go': Arvind Kejriwal urges public to join October 10 protest
Article Text:
Arvind Kejriwal has called for a large-scale protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10

Article Title: ‘Kal aa rahe hain hum’: CJP leaders mock PM Modi as Railways cancels several trains

CJP plans protest despite police denial

Entry, exit gates at 57 Metro stations to remain closed

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) activist Abhijeet Dipke has mocked the Centre over railway cancellations and the closure of entry and exit gates at 57 Metro stations ahead of the organisation's planned protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10, sharing a video in which he and fellow activists Saurabh Das and Ashutosh Ranka are seen laughing about the security measures.In the video, the three appear to be travelling with backpacks and luggage. Dipke takes a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the restrictions, while the group jokes about the disruption to public transport ahead of Saturday's demonstration.“Abhi humare Vishwa Guru, 56-inch ke maha-manav ji ne railways band kar diye, kyunki kal hum protest karne ja rahe hain,” Dipke says in the video, drawing laughter from the others.He then turns to Saurabh Das and asks what he has to say about the situation. Das responds with a chef's-kiss gesture, suggesting approval of the measures, before saying, “Modi ji jo mahaul banane ja rahe hain, woh... too good.”Ashutosh Ranka joins in, saying, “Bhai, Modi ji, tabiyat toh theek hai aapki? Dikkat toh nahi ho rahi na zyada?”Dipke then returns to the theme of the restrictions, saying, “Blood pressure check karte raho na time to time.Railways band kar di seedha.”Das compares the measures with the restrictions imposed during the Emergency, saying, “Emergency ke time bhi itna band nahi kiya tha, Indira Gandhi the dictator.”Ranka adds another jibe, saying that while right-wing supporters claim people are not turning up in Delhi, the government has restricted transport ahead of the protest. Delhi bandh ka elaan kar diya Government of India ne.”Ranka subsequently makes a reference to General Reginald Dyer, the British officer associated with the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, as the three continue their exchange.The video ends with Dipke saying, “Koi baat nahi, sir. Arrest me, detain me! Saurabh is ready, Ashutosh is ready,” he said in an earlier statement.

Article Title: ‘Prepare for the storm’: Delhi top cop calls for restraint ahead of CJP protest, deploys over 25,000 central force personnel
Article Text:
Delhi Police is preparing for a large protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party on October 10.

Barricades at borders, CCTV surveillance





NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has urged its personnel to exercise restraint and use minimum force while handling crowds ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) proposed protest in the capital on October 10, with around 23,000 additional Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) personnel being made available for deployment.“Prepare for the storm. Practise restraint. Protect the peace. Because the true strength of the police is not merely in controlling a crowd, but in doing so with discipline, dignity and minimum force,” Madhur Verma, Joint Commissioner of Police (Central Range), said in a post on X on Friday.The Ministry of Home Affairs has made around 23,000 CAPF personnel available to Delhi Police for deployment between October 8 and 12, officials said. The additional deployment will take the number of central force personnel in the capital to over 25,000.The heightened security arrangements come amid demonstrations demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Delhi Police has denied permission for the CJP’s proposed protest at Jantar Mantar, citing violations of rules during an earlier demonstration, a senior officer said on Friday.According to the officer, police received the application seeking permission on October 7, just three days before the planned protest, whereas the rules require applications to be submitted at least 10 days in advance.Metro curbs, liquor shop closuresAs part of precautionary measures, the Delhi government has ordered liquor shops to remain closed on October 9 and 10, citing the prevailing situation and the need to maintain public order. The Excise Department said the decision was based on inputs from Delhi Police.Police have also proposed closing the entry and exit gates of 57 metro stations and reducing train frequency over concerns about “unruly crowd movement towards sensitive locations”.In a letter dated October 8, the Joint Commissioner of Police (Transport Range) asked the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation to implement the proposed measures.Delhi Police is putting in place multi-layered barricading and enhanced surveillance to manage the situation. CCTV cameras will monitor developments from control rooms, while face-recognition cameras will also be deployed across the capital, officials said.Vigilance has been stepped up at the city's borders, including Ghazipur, Chilla, Tikri, Singhu, Gurugram, Kapashera, Loni and Badarpur, to monitor the movement of people and vehicles entering Delhi, they added.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) proposed protest in the capital on October 10. 23,000 additional Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) personnel being made available for deployment. Delhi government orders liquor shops to remain closed on October 9 and 10.

Article Title: Is Delhi bandh tomorrow? CJP protest triggers train cancellations, Metro curbs proposed; here's all you need to know
Article Text:
Delhi will see planned protests on October 10, causing significant travel disruptions for residents and commuters

Railways cancels trains over congestion concerns

Delhi Police seeks restrictions at 57 Metro stations

Delhi Police denies permission for CJP protest

Security tightened at Delhi borders

Liquor shops to remain shut for two days





NEW DELHI: A proposed protest by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) and other groups in Delhi on October 10 has prompted a security clampdown, with Indian Railways cancelling several trains, Delhi Police seeking restrictions at 57 Metro stations and security being stepped up at the city's borders.However, there has been no announcement of a blanket bandh across the capital.The protest, called over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demanding accountability from Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, has been denied permission by Delhi Police.The police cited short notice, alleged violations during an earlier demonstration and concerns over public safety, law and order and traffic management.The measures are expected to affect commuters travelling through central Delhi and those arriving at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations on Saturday.Indian Railways has decided to cancel Mail and Express trains scheduled to arrive at New Delhi and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway stations between 4am and 2pm on October 10.Trains departing from their originating stations after 2pm on October 9 and scheduled to reach either station during this window on October 10 will be cancelled at source, railway sources said.The decision follows intelligence inputs and traffic advisories warning of severe congestion around the two stations. Officials said the precautionary measure was aimed at ensuring passenger safety and preventing inconvenience caused by traffic disruptions.Separately, West Central Railway's Bhopal division announced the cancellation of the Mumbai–Hazrat Nizamuddin Rajdhani Express (22221) on October 9 due to operational reasons.Passengers have been advised to check official railway updates before travelling.Delhi Police has asked the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) to close entry and exit gates at 57 Metro stations from 9pm on October 9 and continue the proposed restrictions on October 10 until the situation normalises.The police have also sought a reduction in train frequency at the identified stations, citing the possibility of unruly crowd movement towards sensitive locations.The stations named in the communication include Rajiv Chowk, Central Secretariat, Patel Chowk, Janpath, New Delhi, Mandi House, ITO, Supreme Court, Indraprastha, Kashmere Gate, Karol Bagh, INA, Hauz Khas, Lajpat Nagar and Jamia Millia Islamia, among others.The request does not by itself confirm that DMRC has approved or implemented the proposed measures. Commuters should check official Metro advisories before travelling.Joint Commissioner of Police Nupur Prasad said the police received an application from CJP co-convener Saurav Das on October 7, just three days before the proposed demonstration at Jantar Mantar.Police guidelines require applications at least 10 days before a planned protest, she said. The police also cited alleged non-compliance with directions and undertakings during an earlier demonstration, as well as concerns over the prevailing law-and-order situation and traffic regulation.Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) is in force in the New Delhi district. Police have warned that unauthorised gatherings and violations of prohibitory orders could invite legal action.Deputy Commissioner of Police Shrishti Pandey urged people not to participate in unauthorised gatherings, cautioning that violations could have legal consequences.Delhi Police has heightened vigilance at Ghazipur, Chilla, Tikri, Singhu, Gurugram, Kapashera, Loni and Badarpur borders ahead of the proposed protest.Police teams have contacted market welfare associations, resident welfare associations and Aman committees in several areas, asking them to counsel people against participating in activities that could disturb public order.Sources said police were also monitoring hotels, railway stations and other transit points, checking last-minute bookings and approaching groups gathered at these locations to inquire about their plans.The proposed demonstration comes amid heightened tensions over protests linked to electoral roll revisions and demands for the Chief Election Commissioner's accountability.Separately, all retail liquor outlets in Delhi will remain closed on October 9 and 10 following an excise department order issued on October 8.The closure covers specified retail outlets selling Indian liquor, foreign liquor and country liquor, including certain outlets in malls. Licensed restaurants, bars and clubs, however, will continue to serve liquor as usual, an excise department official said.With train cancellations, possible Metro restrictions and enhanced security measures in place, commuters have been advised to monitor official advisories and allow additional time for travel on October 10.
Article Summary: Protest by Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) and other groups in Delhi on October 10. Indian Railways cancels several trains, Delhi Police seeking restrictions at 57 Metro stations. Security stepped up at Delhi borders ahead of the planned protest.

Article Title: A hiker went missing on Arkansas' Eagle Rock Loop; a stranger took a day off to find him, and now his family has launched a GoFundMe to thank her
Article Text:
Ashley Lea Smith is pictured with her dog, Buckey, and Matt Teeters after the missing hiker was found on Arkansas' Eagle Rock Loop. Photo credit: GoFundMe/Family.

How a stranger and her dog found the missing hiker in Arkansas

Why the family launched a GoFundMe for the rescuer

Ashley Smith says she was simply trying to do the right thing

What happened during the search for Matt Teeters?

Where the GoFundMe donations will go

A missing hiker in Arkansas was found after a stranger took a day off work and joined the search with her dog, prompting his family to launch a GoFundMe campaign to thank the pair. Matt Teeters disappeared on September 23, 2026, while hiking the Eagle Rock Loop in the Ouachita National Forest after becoming separated from his cousin. As search efforts continued overnight, Ashley Lea Smith, a local hiker familiar with the terrain, decided to look for him the following morning. Accompanied by her dog, Buckey, Smith eventually located Teeters near Winding Stair. He was reunited with his family after first responders checked him for injuries. His family later launched an online fundraiser to help pay for repairs and improvements to Smith's home.Teeters was hiking the Eagle Rock Loop near Albert Pike in Arkansas when he became separated from his cousin, Nick Walker, on September 23. According to local reporting, the pair were approaching Winding Stair, where a relative was expected to meet them with additional water and Gatorade.Teeters was walking behind Walker because his feet were blistered and he had slowed down. Walker reached the meeting point, but Teeters did not arrive.After searching the surrounding area without finding him, the family contacted authorities, and an emergency signal was sent using satellite messaging.The disappearance prompted a search led by the Montgomery County Sheriff's Office, with assistance from the US Forest Service. Search efforts continued into the night as rescuers worked to locate Teeters in the mountainous terrain.News of the missing hiker eventually reached Ashley Lea Smith, who was familiar with the area through her hiking experience. On the morning of September 24, she called in to work, took her dog Buckey and headed towards the Winding Stair area to look for him.Smith approached from Musgrove Hole and eventually spotted a man wearing a red shirt. In an interview with local television station KTHV, she recalled calling out to ask whether he was Matt.When he confirmed his identity, Smith told her dog, “Buckey, we found him.”Teeters was subsequently reunited with his cousin and family. Smith told KTHV that emergency medical personnel and other first responders examined him and found that he had scrapes and bruises. He was otherwise reported to be OK.After Teeters was found, his family decided to organise a fundraiser to express their gratitude to Smith for taking the time to search for someone she had never met.The GoFundMe campaign, titled Giving Back to Ashley and Buckey - Hiking Heroes, was organised by Jennifer Teeters, Matt's sister. According to the campaign description, the family wanted to help Smith with repairs and improvements to her home, including work on the roof and the construction of a new deck.The family contributed the first $500 towards the cost of materials, labour and other expenses associated with the work. In its appeal, the family explained that Smith had provided the news they had spent the night hoping and praying for.The fundraiser was intended as a way to offer practical assistance in return for her kindness. Smith had not asked for a reward, and the family described the campaign as an opportunity to support someone who had stepped forward when they needed help.According to People, the campaign had raised more than $6,000 by October 2, 2026, towards its stated goal at the time. Fundraising totals can change, and the amount raised should be checked against the live campaign page before publication.Despite the attention surrounding the rescue, Smith played down the idea that she had done anything extraordinary.Speaking to KTHV, she said she did not consider herself special and described her decision as an attempt to help someone in need. She also credited Buckey for accompanying her during the search.Smith's actions came after an overnight search involving authorities and other searchers. Her familiarity with the area helped her decide where to look, and she eventually located Teeters near Winding Stair.The rescue also brought relief to Teeters' relatives, who had spent hours uncertain about his whereabouts. Jennifer Teeters wrote in the fundraiser description that the family would never be able to fully repay Smith for the relief she brought them.The campaign has therefore become more than a fundraising appeal. It is an attempt by a family to offer tangible support to a stranger whose decision to help made a lasting difference to them.The Eagle Rock Loop is a roughly 27-mile hiking route in Arkansas' Ouachita National Forest. Teeters had set out on the hike with his cousin, and the pair became separated while making their way along the trail.According to accounts shared by the family and local reporting, Teeters took a wrong turn near a trail junction and became lost. Searchers worked through the night, with the rugged terrain complicating communications and the effort to locate him.The incident also prompted online speculation about whether the cousins had argued or whether Teeters had been abandoned. His cousin rejected those claims, and the available reporting indicates that the separation occurred during the hike.Teeters was eventually found on September 24, and the family was able to reunite with him after the search. The subsequent GoFundMe campaign shifted attention towards Smith and Buckey, whose contribution the family wanted to recognise.The fundraiser is intended to help cover improvements to Smith's home, particularly a new deck and roof repairs. Jennifer Teeters said the family wanted to support Smith in the same spirit in which she had helped them.The initial $500 contribution came from the family itself, with the online appeal inviting other people to contribute towards the remaining costs.The campaign's stated purpose is to fund the repairs and upgrades, rather than to provide Smith with a general cash reward.
Article Summary: Matt Teeters disappeared on September 23, 2026, while hiking the Eagle Rock Loop in the Ouachita National Forest in Arkansas. Local hiker Ashley Lea Smith took a day off work and joined the search the following morning. She eventually located Teeters near Winding Stair and he was reunited with his family. His family later launched an online fundraiser to help pay for repairs and improvements to Smith's home.

Article Title: Navi Pillay's Nobel Peace Prize puts focus back on 2 landmark Rwanda genocide cases
Article Text:
Navi Pillay served on the ICT from 1995 to 2003, including four years as its president.

Recognised rape as an act of genocide

Five key events from a 100-day killing spree

Media Case held propagandists accountable

ALSO READ |

Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, South African jurist of Indian origin, has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her contributions to international justice and human rights , bringing renewed attention to two landmark judgments she helped deliver at the United Nations International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (ICTR).Pillay served as a judge at the tribunal from 1995 to 2003 and was its president from 1999 to 2003. Among the most consequential cases during her tenure were the 1998 trial of Rwandan mayor Jean-Paul Akayesu and the 2003 Media Case, which examined how radio broadcasts and newspaper articles helped incite the 1994 genocide.In 1998, the ICTR convicted Jean-Paul Akayesu, the mayor of Taba in Rwanda, of genocide for his role in violence against the Tutsi population. The case examined his involvement in inciting killings, rape and torture during the genocide, in which at least 800,000 people were killed.Akayesu became the first person to be convicted of genocide by an international court. The judgment also established that rape and sexual violence could constitute acts of genocide when committed with the intention of destroying a protected group, in whole or in part.The ruling was significant because sexual violence had often been overlooked in the prosecution of wartime atrocities.It recognised that rape could be used deliberately to destroy a targeted community rather than being treated merely as a consequence of conflict.Pillay was one of the three judges who signed the judgment and was credited with helping shape its reasoning on sexual violence.“From time immemorial, rape has been regarded as spoils of war. Now it will be considered a war crime. We want to send out a strong signal that rape is no longer a trophy of war,” Pillay said after the verdict.In 2003, the tribunal delivered another landmark judgment examining how media organisations and political messaging contributed to the genocide.The case involved Ferdinand Nahimana, a founder of Radio Télévision des Mille Collines (RTLM), Hassan Ngeze, editor-in-chief of the newspaper Kangura, and Jean-Bosco Barayagwiza, a board member of RTLM’s initiating committee and a founding member of the Coalition for the Defence of the Republic.The tribunal found the three guilty of crimes including genocide, incitement to genocide and crimes against humanity. Nahimana and Ngeze were sentenced to life imprisonment, while Barayagwiza received a 35-year prison sentence.The judgment examined how RTLM broadcasts and Kangura articles spread hatred against Tutsis and encouraged violence. It also considered propaganda that portrayed Tutsi women as “seductive agents of the enemy”.Pillay presided over the case alongside judges Erik Møse and Asoka de Zoysa Gunawardana. The ruling established that people who used media platforms to incite genocide could be held criminally responsible for their actions.“You were fully aware of the power of words, and you used the radio, the medium of communication with the widest public reach to disseminate hatred and violence,” Pillay told Nahimana while delivering the ruling.She added, “Without a firearm, machete or any physical weapon, you caused the death of thousands of innocent civilians.”Pillay also said, “The power of the media to create and destroy fundamental human values comes with great responsibility. Those who control such media are accountable for its consequences”.The two judgments addressed different dimensions of the Rwandan genocide. The Akayesu ruling recognised sexual violence as a possible means of committing genocide, while the Media Case established legal accountability for using communications platforms to incite mass violence.
Article Summary: Navanethem “Navi’ Pillay, South African jurist of Indian origin, has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her contributions to international justice and human rights. Pillay served as a judge at the tribunal from 1995 to 2003 and was its president from 1999 to 2003. Among the most consequential cases during her tenure were the 1998 trial of Rwandan mayor Jean-Paul Akayesu and the 2003 Media Case.
